verdicts.reasoning: Proposed 'certification' is the procedural act/filing of certifying a case trial-ready (akin to note of issue), whereas candidate 'Certificate (Litigation)' is a written proof-of-fact document and 'Ratification' concerns approving another's acts — labels overlap but definitions differ.
Proposed 'interrogatory' (singular) matches candidate 'Interrogatories' — both are written questions posed by one party to another in discovery, so this is the same concept differing only in number.

Proposed 'dates' refers to calendar dates as facts in an evidence summary, while candidate 'date' is defined narrowly as a technical data-segment field element, so the definitions do not describe the same modeled concept.

Proposed 'Record Proceedings' means having a reporter make a stenographic record, whereas all candidates (Proceeding Removed/Reopened/Transferred/Reactivated) describe changes in case status — the shared word 'Proceeding' is coincidental.

Proposed 'Trial Documents' means documents produced/used at trial, but candidates 'Travel Document', 'Tax Documents', 'Real Estate Documents', and 'Document ID' each define unrelated document types — only the word 'Document' is shared.

Proposed 'Administrative Notice' is notice taken by an administrative tribunal (parallel to judicial notice), while candidates 'Administrative Mandate/Order/Negligence/Discharge' define unrelated administrative acts — the 'Administrative' prefix is coincidental.

Proposed 'Civil Conduct' concerns advocate civility/professional decorum, whereas candidates 'Civil Court', 'Civil Contempt', and 'Civil Contract Law' define unrelated concepts — the 'Civil' label is coincidental.

Proposed 'omissions' means points left out of an argument, while candidates 'Commission' (a governing body), 'Admission', and 'Commissions (Pay)' are semantically unrelated despite orthographic similarity.

Proposed 'case background' means the factual/procedural background of a matter, whereas candidate 'Background Check' is an investigation of an individual's history — the shared word 'background' is coincidental.
Proposed 'elicitation' means drawing out a witness's testimony on direct, while candidate 'Solicitation' is the crime of encouraging another to commit an offense — a purely phonetic collision.
Proposed 'assigned' (a successor judge assigned by the clerk) matches candidate 'Assignment', defined as designating a specific case or judge to handle a legal matter, so it names the same concept.

Proposed 'new matter' means a new topic raised during witness examination, while candidates 'MATTER_NAME', 'matter_net_exp', and 'Matter Net Fees' are billing/case-record fields using 'matter' in the sense of a legal case — an unrelated sense.

Proposed 'summary judgment motions' is the same concept as candidate 'Motion for Summary Judgment' — a request that the court rule in a party's favor without trial based on the evidence — differing only in plural/word order.
Proposed 'deny motion' means a ruling denying a motion, whereas candidates 'Demotion', 'Emotion', and 'Demolition' are wholly unrelated words that merely resemble the phrase phonetically.

Proposed 'litigation expense' means the cost of litigating, while candidates 'Litigation Defenses', 'Litigation Events', and 'Litigation Agreements' define unrelated litigation concepts — the 'Litigation' prefix is coincidental.

Proposed 'conduct codes' is a word-order variant of candidate 'Code of Conduct', both defined as written guidelines of ethical principles and proper practices expected of individuals — the same concept.
Proposed 'trial pace' means the speed/tempo of a trial, whereas candidate 'Trial Practice' is the body of skills and procedures for presenting a case — the shared 'Trial' root is coincidental.

Proposed 'concessions' means yielded/admitted points in argument, while candidates 'Confession', 'Concussion', and 'Contusion' define an admission of guilt and brain injuries respectively — pure phonetic collisions.

Proposed 'request admission' means requesting that noticed evidence be admitted, whereas candidate 'Requests for Admission' is the pretrial discovery device asking an opponent to admit or deny facts — a coincidental label collision between two different procedures.

Proposed 'litigation deadlines' means time limits/dates in a case, while candidates 'Litigation Defenses', 'Litigation Identifiers', and 'Litigation Events' define unrelated litigation concepts — only the 'Litigation' prefix matches.

Proposed 'motion to deny' (a request that a movant's motion be denied) does not match any candidate; 'Motion to Amend', 'Motion to Hear', 'Motion to File', and 'Motion to Abandon' are all distinct, unrelated motion types.

Proposed 'evidence introduction' is the general procedural act of introducing evidence, whereas candidate 'Motion to Introduce Evidence' is a specific formal request — the act differs from the motion, and other candidates are evidence subtypes.

Proposed 'substantive evidence' means evidence offered to prove the truth of a matter (versus impeachment), whereas the near-identical-label candidate 'Substantial Evidence' denotes a quantum/standard of proof — the definitions describe different things.

Proposed 'Oral opposition' is spoken opposition to a motion at a hearing, whereas candidate 'Opposition / Reply' is defined as a written response filed in court — a different medium, making this a distinct (oral) form rather than a merge.

Proposed 'statutory rules' means procedural rules established by statute, while candidates 'Statutory Rape', 'Statutory Lien', and 'Statutory Fraud' define unrelated statutory concepts — only the 'Statutory' prefix is shared.

Proposed 'administrative relief' means relief sought from an administrative tribunal, whereas candidates 'Administrative Order', 'Administrative Negligence', and 'Administrative Law Judge' define unrelated administrative concepts — the prefix match is coincidental.

Proposed 'interjection' means an interrupting remark to avoid during proceedings, while candidates 'Intervention', 'Insurrection', 'Injunction', and 'Infraction' are unrelated legal terms sharing only a similar sound.

Proposed 'Motion to recuse/disqualify judge' matches candidate 'Motion to Disqualify Judge', both defined as a request to remove a judge from a case for conflict of interest or bias — the same concept.

Proposed 'Certificate of Prejudice' is a certificate-form instrument to remove a judge, distinct from candidate 'Affidavit of Prejudice' which is specifically a sworn affidavit; the source itself lists 'certificate/affidavit' as alternative instruments, so this is a distinct FOLIO gap.
Proposed 'phrases' (key words/phrases to emphasize) has no definitional match; candidates 'Phrae', 'Horses', 'Radishes', and 'Pheasants' are unrelated place names and animals/plants.

Proposed 'agreement on facts' means a stipulation of facts, whereas candidates 'Factoring Agreement', 'Formation Agreement', 'Mediation Agreement', and 'Franchise Agreement' are all substantive commercial contracts — only the word 'agreement' is shared.

Proposed 'Use of Evidence' is the act/practice of presenting and using evidence, whereas candidate 'Rules of Evidence' denotes the procedural rules governing evidence — related but definitionally distinct.

Proposed 'Judicial Role' concerns a judge's conception of their function, while candidates 'Judicial Lien', 'Judicial Order', 'Judicial Privilege', and 'Res Judicata' define unrelated concepts — the 'Judicial' prefix is coincidental.

Proposed 'contract case' means a lawsuit arising from a contract, whereas candidates 'Contractual Clause', 'Contract Year Clause', and 'Counterpart Clause' are contract provisions — the shared 'contract' root is coincidental.

Proposed 'administrative hearing officer' is the non-ALJ role that presides over administrative hearings, whereas candidate 'Chief Administrative Officer' is a corporate executive and 'Office of the Chief Administrative Hearing Officer' is a specific federal agency — neither defines this presiding-officer role.
Proposed 'dismiss' (as a dispositive move terminating a case) names the same concept as candidate 'Dismissal', defined as terminating a case without a decision on the merits.

Proposed 'Electronic Information' means digital/electronically stored information, whereas candidates 'Genetic Information', 'Contact Information', and 'Electric Power Generation' are unrelated despite the shared 'Information'/'Electric' tokens.
Proposed 'amended' (pleadings amended to conform to evidence) has no definitional match; candidates 'Mende', 'Mubende', 'Agender', and 'Kamwenge' are a language, places, and a gender identity.

Proposed 'Personal service' means personal service of process on a party, whereas candidates 'Personal Care Services', 'Other Personal Services', and 'Postal Service' are NAICS-style industry categories — a coincidental 'service' collision.

Proposed 'evidence processing' means the logistical handling of evidence to ensure admissibility, whereas candidates 'Impression Evidence', 'Forensic Evidence', and 'Shoeprint Evidence' are forensic evidence types — a coincidental 'evidence' overlap.
Proposed 'places' (geographic locations subject to judicial notice) has no definitional match; candidates 'Laches', 'Lacs', 'Peaches', and 'Lakes' are a legal defense, water bodies, and a fruit.

Proposed 'Mistrial motions' matches candidate 'Motion for Mistrial', both defined as a request during trial to declare the proceedings invalid due to significant error or misconduct — the same concept.

Proposed 'positions' means argumentative stances to emphasize, whereas candidates 'Deposition', 'Prostitution', 'Motions', and 'Constitutions' are unrelated concepts sharing only orthographic fragments.
Proposed 'judge assignment method' names the process of assigning a judge, matching candidate 'Assignment of Judge', defined as the process of designating a judge to preside over a particular case.

Proposed 'non-evidentiary motion' is a motion that does NOT concern evidence, the negation of candidate 'Evidentiary Motions' (motions to admit or exclude evidence) — the labels overlap but the definitions are opposites.

Proposed 'advisement' means a court taking a matter under consideration before ruling, whereas candidate 'Advertisement' is a promotional copyright work — a phonetic collision, and other candidates are unrelated.
Proposed 'object' is the act of raising an objection, whereas candidate 'Objector' is defined as the person who objects and 'Objectives' as goals — the act differs from both the actor and the aims.

Proposed 'Motion Documents' means the set of documents comprising a motion, whereas candidates 'Document Location', 'Objection Document', 'Motion to File Document', and 'Tax Documents' define unrelated document concepts.
Proposed 'main' (a type of court calendar) has no definitional match; candidates 'Maine', 'Mardin', 'Oman', and 'Maio' are all places.

Proposed 'judicial relief' means relief granted by a court, whereas candidates 'Judicial Lien', 'Judicial Order', and 'Judicial Privilege' define unrelated concepts and 'Equitable Relief' is a specific relief type — none matches the general concept.

Proposed 'presentation notes' means an advocate's notes/outline used as a speaking guide, whereas candidate 'Presentation' is the persuasive account itself and 'L680 Presentation' is an ESI-display billing activity — the notes differ from the presentation.

Proposed 'Oral motion' is a motion made orally (per FRCP 7(b)), whereas candidates 'Trial Motions', 'Post-Trial Motions', and 'Pretrial Motions' classify motions by timing, not by oral/written manner — none captures the oral-form concept.

Proposed 'CAT' is Computer-Aided Transcription, an alternative to court reporters, whereas candidates 'Cats', 'Cavite', 'Cattle', and 'Car' are animals, a province, and a vehicle — the acronym coincides with unrelated labels.
